system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Graph-regularised pseudo-masks: CRF smoothing on the patch grid for mask-free MVFA training
SUMMARY: Clean label-restricted pseudo-masks with a fully connected CRF over patches whose unary term is the NN-distance score and whose pairwise term uses CLIP feature similarity and position.
HYPOTHESIS: CRF regularisation reduces isolated false-positive components in pseudo-masks by at least 50% and increases pseudo-mask Dice by at least 6 points, and MVFA trained on CRF-regularised pseudo-masks attains higher pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities than MVFA trained on raw pseudo-masks.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: target type: true masks; raw label-restricted pseudo-masks; CRF-regularised pseudo-masks with pairwise weight w in {1, 3, 5}. Unary: u_p = -log sigmoid((d_p - t_hi)/s), with s the std of normal-to-normal distances; pairwise: Potts with kernel w exp(-|x_p - x_q|^2/(2 theta_x^2) - (1 - cos(f_p, f_q))/theta_f), theta_x = 3 patches, theta_f = 0.1; mean-field inference, 10 iterations, on the 17x17 grid. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask Dice, false-positive components per normal-appearing region, trained pixel AUROC and Dice.
RATIONALE: Label-restricted pseudo-masks contain isolated false positives (healthy but rare anatomy) and holes inside lesions. G-Anomaly shows that modelling the topology of image regions separates anomalies from normal texture. A pairwise graph model over patches (a dense CRF on the patch grid with feature and spatial affinities) can enforce that anomalous patches form coherent regions, removing isolated false positives and filling holes before the masks supervise MVFA.
METHOD: 1) make_pseudo_masks.py: compute d_p and the label-restricted rule. 2) crf_refine.py: implement mean-field inference for a fully connected Potts CRF on 289 patches in PyTorch (dense 289x289 kernel, cheap). 3) Output q_p = P(anomalous); mask = q_p > 0.5, upsampled to 240 px; abnormal images only. 4) dataset/medical_zero.py loads the refined masks; train_zero.py unchanged. 5) w selected on source validation where source masks exist. Hyper-parameters: theta_x 3, theta_f 0.1, 10 iterations, MVFA training as in the paper.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on the masked targets BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Checkpoints and all thresholds selected on source-modality validation splits only; MVFA re-run under the same rule as the mask-supervised reference; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; raw pseudo-masks; CRF with w in {1,3,5}; masks removed from 1 and 3 sources. Ablation: spatial-only kernel vs spatial+feature kernel. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice, isolated FP components, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if CRF masks do not reduce isolated components by half or if trained pixel AUROC does not improve.

Idea B:
TITLE: Context-prediction residual pseudo-masks: a normal-trained masked-feature predictor localises lesions
SUMMARY: Train a small transformer on normal source images to predict a masked patch's CLIP feature from its surrounding patches, and use the prediction residual on abnormal images as a context-aware pseudo-mask for MVFA's segmentation branch.
HYPOTHESIS: Pseudo-masks from the context-prediction residual reach at least 10 points higher Dice against true masks than nearest-neighbour pseudo-masks on BrainMRI and LiverCT, where anatomy varies with position, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: The inspiring idea spreads evidence over a structural affinity graph. A different analogy comes from inpainting and from radiologists' reading: a region is abnormal when it is not what its surroundings predict. Nearest-neighbour pseudo-masks ignore context, so a normal structure that is rare in the bank (e.g. ventricles at an unusual slice) is flagged, while a lesion that resembles normal tissue elsewhere is missed. A model that predicts each patch's feature from its context, trained only on normal images, captures anatomy-conditional normality; its residual is a context-aware anomaly score. Training is cheap because it operates on frozen 17x17 CLIP feature grids, not pixels.
METHOD: 1) Extract frozen CLIP layer-24 patch features (17x17x1024) for all normal source training images. 2) Predictor: 4-layer transformer (width 256, 8 heads) with learned 2-D position embeddings; input = feature grid with 15% of patches replaced by a mask token (block masking, 3x3 blocks); output = predicted features at masked positions; loss = 1 - cosine. Train 30 epochs, AdamW lr 3e-4, batch 64 (minutes on one GPU). 3) Residual r_p = 1 - cos(f_p, f_hat_p) with each patch masked once (sliding 3x3 block masking, averaged). 4) Threshold at the 99th percentile of residuals on normal source-validation images; label-restricted to abnormal images. 5) dataset/medical_zero.py loads masks; train_zero.py unchanged. Hyper-parameters as stated; MVFA training as in the paper.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; NN pseudo-masks; context-residual pseudo-masks; their union and intersection. Masks removed from all 3 masked sources. Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice per dataset, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if residual pseudo-masks do not beat NN pseudo-masks by 10 Dice points on BrainMRI or LiverCT.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>

CONFIDENCE: HIGH
